e: At least 11 people are detained following a pro-Palestinian demonstration in Tunis.
Amid deadly blackouts, protests erupt on the fifth anniversary of the 2021 Tunisian self-coup and continue for days afterward.
The town of Sidi Bou Saïd is designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
President Kais Saied is admitted to a hospital for an emergency procedure after suffering a heart attack.
A court sentences journalist Khaoula Boukrim to four years' imprisonment in absentia under Decree-Law 54, after she had fled to Paris in December 2025.
The Tunis Court of First Instance sentences Ennahda leader Rached Ghannouchi to life imprisonment on charges of terrorism.

President Saied dismisses Energy Minister Fatma Thabet amid controversy over planned renewable energy projects ahead of a parliamentary vote; Salah Zouari is appointed to temporarily oversee the ministry.
Journalist Zied Heni is detained by order of the public prosecutor, after publishing an article critical of the judiciary. He is sentenced to 1 year in prison on 7 May.
Authorities order a one-month suspension of the Tunisian Human Rights League, a civil society organization and member of the Tunisian National Dialogue Quartet.
A court sentences comedian and actor Lotfi Abdelli in absentia to 18 months’ imprisonment on charges including insulting state officials and offending public morality.
A court sentences journalist Ghassen Ben Khelifa to two years in prison on charges of publishing fake news.
A court sentences migrant rights activist Saadia Mosbah to eight years in prison, on charges of money laundering and illicit enrichment.

A court jails businessman Marouan Mabrouk for corruption, while former prime minister Youssef Chahed and several ex-cabinet members are sentenced in absentia to six years in prison and fined $800 million for their handling of Mabrouk’s case.
Former prime minister Ali Laarayedh is jailed for 24 years for aiding the travel of Tunisian jihadists to Syria; seven others are also sentenced in the trial.
Five people are sentenced to up to 15 years' imprisonment on charges of involvement in the 2023 Djerba synagogue shooting.

Police detain opposition figure Olfa Hamdi, leader of the Third Republic party, upon her arrival at Tunis–Carthage International Airport, after calling for a transitional government, and early elections.
President Saied extends the national state of emergency by 11 months, through 31 December 2026.
A court in Tunis sentences journalists Bohran Bssaies and Mourad Zghidi to 3.5 years imprisonment on charges of money laundering.
At least four people are killed in flooding in Monastir Governorate, the worst floods since 1950.
